headline: Lowest ozone reading in the city sits next to zero mapped gardens in Ward 29.
summary:
Ward 29 sits on Chicago's West Side, taking in Austin, Montclare, Dunning, and Belmont Cragin. Its composite score of 35.2 lands it 38th out of 50, in the bottom third of the city. Air quality and a quick-moving 311 system are what stand out first. Chicago 311 closes graffiti requests here almost immediately, and the ward posts the lowest average ozone reading of the fifty on one air-quality measure, with a similarly strong showing on a second, separate measure that ranks seventh.

Outdoor space and upkeep are where the numbers turn weaker. Mapped gardens, registered murals, and distance to the lake all sit near the foot of the list, half of the ward's park drinking fountains have tested positive for elevated lead at some point, and pothole repairs run slower here than almost anywhere else in the city.
reading_the_rankings: Take the camera-spending share, which ranks 2nd out of 50 at 0.2 percent of the ward's menu money. The middle band of that scale is under a single point wide citywide, so nearly the whole city sits at a similarly low share, and a rank of 2 says less than it looks like. The wastewater proximity score, a measure of industrial pollution near local streams, ranks 3rd out of 50, but a two-point slice of that scale holds thirty-five wards, and this ward is one of them, so the ranking here reads sharper than the real gap behind it. The estimate itself comes from working out how big a piece of each nearby tract sits inside the 29th's boundary, so a wedge of a bordering tract's number can land here even though the ward does not reach that tract directly. The garden count runs the other way. It ranks 47th with zero gardens mapped, but a two-point band on that scale holds eighteen wards, including this one, so the sharp-looking rank sits on top of a fairly small real gap.
